job.title: Customer Service Specialist
job.description:
About the Company

Our client is a national leader in commercial services. With a strong national footprint and a genuine focus on developing internal talent, they're growing their commercial team and looking for someone ready to build a long-term career in customer service & account management.


About the Role

This is a fantastic opportunity for someone with a background in sales administration or customer service who is looking to fast-track their career toward a Account Manager role. You'll be the primary point of contact for a portfolio of national and cross-regional clients, working closely with National Account Managers to keep service, pricing and communication running smoothly.

Day to day, you'll:
  • Build strong relationships with key customer stakeholders and manage regular contact cycles
  • Resolve customer queries on pricing, service, accounts and invoicing
  • Maintain accurate customer data and documentation across internal systems
  • Coordinate service delivery with branch operations and support teams
  • Support renewals, contract variations and quotes alongside National Account Managers
  • Produce weekly and monthly reporting on customer service activity and performance
This role has been specifically designed as a stepping stone into account management — genuine progression is on the table for the right person.

About You
  • You aspire to grow into an Account Manager role and want to be backed to get there
  • Strong communicator, confident building relationships with internal and external stakeholders
  • Excellent attention to detail and administrative accuracy
  • Strong Excel skills
  • Prior experience in sales administration, customer service or a coordination role
  • Comfortable managing competing priorities in a fast-paced commercial environment
If you're looking for a genuine career pathway into account management, backed by a supportive national business, we'd love to hear from you.

Key Benefits
  • Attractive Salary Package 
  • Car parking provided
  • Strong mentorship from an experienced Leaders
  • Clear pathway into Key Account Management
  • Collaborative national business with strong internal support

job.title: Digital Marketing Manager
job.description:
About the Company
 
They are fast-scaling, PE-backed business operating in the property and travel technology space, managing a large national portfolio built through a series of acquisitions. Right now, that portfolio runs across fragmented systems inherited through M&A, before they can execute an effective national marketing strategy, we need to build the foundation underneath it.
 
The marketing function is entering an exciting build phase and they're looking for a Digital Marketing Manager to help lead the charge.
 
About the Role
 
This is a genuine build-phase seat, not a pure campaign execution role. Your first 6-12 months will be spent laying the groundwork, domain migration, website rebuild, and building out the data and CRM infrastructure that the business needs before it can market effectively. Once that foundation is in place, you'll move into owning national and local campaign execution across multiple audiences.
 
You won't be doing the technical build yourself, you will work closely with the technology team, but you'll be the digital marketing voice in the room, shaping what "good" looks like, choosing the right tools, and making sure the foundation is built with commercial marketing outcomes in mind.
 
What You'll Be Doing
 
  • Support the migration from a legacy domain to a new national domain, working closely with the technical team to protect SEO equity through the transition
  • Play a key role in the website rebuild project, site architecture, and platform decisions
  • Help stand up a proper CRM and centralised data layer, the business currently has no single source of truth for its customer database, so this is genuinely ground-up work
  • Working with the internal insights team to connect valuable portfolio-level data back to customers in a meaningful way
  • Have a seat at the table on martech tool selection (CRM platform, marketing automation, etc.) — you don't need to build it, but you need to know what "good" looks like
  • Own execution of national marketing campaigns across performance channels (paid social, search, programmatic)
  • Run local/regional campaigns tailored to different markets, this is a business with genuine geographic nuance, where messaging that works in one state may be completely wrong in another
 
About You
  • Solid experience in a digital marketing management role, ideally gained in a scale-up, startup, or high-growth environment, comfort with ambiguity and a "build it as we go" mindset is essential
  • Exposure to CRM platforms (HubSpot or similar) and an understanding of what a modern martech stack should look like, even if you haven't built one yourself
  • SEO fundamentals, particularly around site migrations and protecting search equity through a domain or platform change
  • A commercially minded approach, able to think about lead generation and audience segmentation, not just channel execution
  • Comfort operating semi-autonomously in a hybrid/remote team, this isn't a role for someone who needs to be managed closely
  • Franchising, multi-site, or portfolio-based business experience is a genuine plus
  • Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills
  • The ability to manage multiple projects and deadlines in a fast-paced environment

job.title: Production Supervisor - Precast Concrete - T2P role
job.description:
About The Company
Our client is a well-established, family-owned manufacturer with over 50 years' history in the design, fabrication, and supply of industrial products used across Australia and internationally. With in-house manufacturing capabilities spanning precast concrete and composite production, the business maintains full control from design through to delivery, a key differentiator in a competitive market.
 
About The Role
We're looking for an experienced Production Supervisor on a temp to perm basis to help lead day-to-day operations at a manufacturing facility near Riverview. You'll take ownership of production output, safety, quality, and people performance on site. 
 
Key responsibilities will include:
  • Leading and developing the site's production team, including direct oversight of the frontline workforce, to ensure consistent output against production schedules and quality benchmarks.
  • Owning site safety performance, embedding a strong safety culture, ensuring WHS compliance, and driving toward zero-harm outcomes.
  • Managing day-to-day production planning and scheduling, ensuring on-time delivery against customer and project timelines.
  • Maintaining quality control standards in line with certified manufacturing processes and product warranty commitments.
  • Managing rostering, resourcing, and performance management across the team, including coaching and developing the staff.
  • Coordinating with procurement, logistics, and warehousing to maintain stock control and ensure materials are available to meet production demand.
  • Driving continuous improvement initiatives across plant efficiency, waste reduction, and process standardisation.
  • Reporting to senior leadership on site performance, capacity planning, and operational risk.
 
About You
You're an experienced manufacturing or production leader who's comfortable being hands-on and knows how to get the best out of a team. You bring genuine credibility on the plant floor and a practical understanding of what it takes to run a site well.
 
You'll likely have:
  • A proven track record in a Site Manager/Supervisor, Production Manager/Supervisor, or Operations Manager role within a manufacturing, fabrication, or industrial production environment.
  • Demonstrated experience leading teams of a similar size (10+)
  • Strong experience within precast concrete manufacturing or a closely related manufacturing or construction environment.
  • A strong working knowledge of WHS compliance and a genuine commitment to safety leadership.
  • Proven experience leading and developing production teams.
  • Strong production planning and scheduling capability.
  • Experience managing labour, resources and competing production priorities.
  • Solid understanding of production planning, scheduling, and quality control processes in a manufacturing setting.
  • Strong communication and people leadership skills, with the ability to coach, motivate, and hold a team accountable in a practical, straightforward way.
  • A continuous improvement mindset, with the confidence to identify and implement process efficiencies.

job.title: Part-Time Bookkeeper - 25 hours a week
job.description:
About The Company 
 
A boutique Chartered Accounting practice based in the heart of the Sydney CBD, dedicated to providing exceptional, hands-on service to a genuinely diverse client base. 
 
Their work goes well beyond standard compliance. They regularly advise clients on financial software implementations, business structuring, and best-practice finance processes, and are known among their clients for being commercially minded rather than just box-ticking accountants. Their systems and workflows are fully cloud-based, which gives their team real flexibility in how and where work gets done, and focus energy on advice and client outcomes rather than administration.
 
They're a small, close-knit team rather than a large corporate practice, which means your work is visible, your contribution matters, and you won't get lost in a big hierarchy.
 
The Opportunity
 
You'll work directly alongside a forward-thinking principal across the entire client portfolio, not siloed into one narrow function, giving you exposure to compliance, advisory, structuring and client relationship management all at once. It's a genuinely collaborative environment, with real opportunities to shape how the practice runs and to grow your own experience faster than you might in a larger firm.
 
We know great accountants come with all kinds of commitments outside work. My client is genuinely open to candidates, including parents balancing school drop-offs and pick-ups, who need a degree of flexibility around core hours.
 
If you can manage your clients, your deadlines and your offshore team effectively, they're far more interested in the quality and reliability of your work than in rigid 9-to-5 attendance. They would rather have the right person working flexibly than the wrong person working standard hours.
 
About The Role
  • Managing your own portfolio of clients directly, ranging from small owner-operated businesses 
  • Acting as a trusted, day-to-day point of contact for clients, building relationships that go beyond transactional compliance work
  • Managing competing deadlines and priorities across a varied portfolio, keeping both clients and the principal informed on status and issues
  • Supervising and reviewing the work of two offshore team members based in the Philippines
  • Approximately 80% of routine compliance preparation is completed offshore, with your role centred on technical review, quality control, coaching, and ensuring everything is accurate and client-ready before it goes out the door, effectively the remaining 20% of the work, but the most critical 20%
  • Providing feedback and on-the-job training to the offshore team to continually lift the standard and consistency of their work
  • Review and, where needed, hands-on completion of BAS, IAS, FBT and SMSF obligations
  • Annual compliance work and income tax returns across a range of entity types
About You
  • CA or CPA qualified
  • Comfortable taking ownership of managing and reviewing the work of offshore team members, including giving clear, constructive feedback
  • Strong client management skills, confident communicating directly with clients, the ATO and ASIC, and comfortable being a client's main point of contact rather than working purely behind the scenes
  • Solid, current working knowledge of relevant tax law (income tax, GST, FBT) and a genuine interest in staying on top of legislative changes as they happen
  • Practical experience with cloud and desktop accounting software, including Xero and MYOB, you should be comfortable and confident, not just familiar
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, you'll be drafting client correspondence and liaising with regulators directly
  • Strong Microsoft Excel skills (comfortable with formulas, reconciliations and reporting), along with confident everyday use of Outlook and Word
  • Reliable, accountable, and comfortable working with a degree of autonomy while staying closely connected to the principal and offshore team

job.title: Head of Retail
job.description:
About The Opportunity

Our client is a well established, premium Australian lifestyle brand with an omni-channel model spanning wholesale, e-commerce and a boutique retail network across NSW and New Zealand. Following a recent restructure of the retail channel, the business is bringing in an experienced, hands-on retail operator to lead a defined performance turnaround ahead of and through the peak trading period.
 
This is a genuine intervention role, not a caretaker position. You will be judged on measurable commercial outcomes within your first weeks on the ground, with strong potential for the engagement to convert to a permanent leadership role for the right person.
 
About They Role 

Reporting directly to the CEO, you will be responsible for restoring store performance to business case levels and lifting the retail channel's contribution ahead of peak trade. This includes:
  • Turning around the network's flagship store, diagnosing and fixing conversion and average transaction value, addressing team capability, floor management and visual and stock presentation, and establishing a daily performance rhythm
  • Embedding operating disciplines across the store network, including industry standard rostering to a wages-to-sales target, stock management, loss prevention and store-level performance reporting
  • Leading retail performance across Australia and New Zealand, with accountability for sales, profitability, productivity, and operational outcomes
  • Developing and executing strategic business plans, forecasts, budgets, and people plans
  • Coaching store managers and teams on the floor in selling skills and product knowledge, building capability that outlasts your engagement
  • Documenting operating routines, rosters and a performance framework the existing team can run going forward
  • Partnering with key stakeholders across Client Relations, Marketing, Human Resources, Merchandising, and Operations to deliver market objectives
  • Maintaining a high-performance culture focused on accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement
About you
  • A proven multi-site retail operator with a track record of turning around underperforming stores, ideally within luxury retail, jewellery, fashion, or a premium customer-focused environment.
  • Hands-on and floor-based by preference, not a head office strategist. You are comfortable being in stores daily, coaching in real time
  • Strong across the fundamentals: rostering economics, conversion levers, stock disciplines and loss prevention
  • Available immediately or at short notice
  • Familiarity with the Australian and New Zealand retail landscape is an advantage but not essential
  • Demonstrated success in developing high-performing leadership teams
  • Exceptional stakeholder management and communication skills
  • Commercially driven and entrepreneurial. You spot the opportunity and move on it.
  • You lead with empathy, honesty and humility, and hold yourself to the standard you set for your teams.
The engagement
  • Reports directly to the CEO
  • Immediate start required, ahead of peak trade
  • Sydney based, with regular presence across the NSW store network and travel to New Zealand as required
This is a rare opportunity to make a fast, visible commercial impact and step into an ongoing leadership role on your own terms. If you have a track record of walking into an underperforming retail network and fixing it, we want to hear from you.

job.title: Head of Sales Operations
job.description:
About The Company
 
Our client is a well established, multi region B2B services business with a national branch network and a strong reputation for reliability and technical service delivery. It's the kind of field based B2B environment where service delivery is executed locally, branch by branch, but where the commercial engine now needs to run nationally to keep pace with the business.
 
The regional model has served the business well operationally. Branches know their customers, their territory and their trade. But sales, process, systems and reporting have all grown up branch by branch alongside it, and that's starting to show. Performance varies significantly from one region to the next, system priorities sit gridlocked between competing local demands, and good, expensive people are spending their time on low value admin instead of selling.
 
About The Role
 
This is a newly created role reporting, with a mandate to build and lead the function that makes the sales organisation effective and consistent nationally. It sits deliberately outside any single region, because process consistency, fair compensation and clean data all break down when Sales Operations is owned regionally rather than centrally. You'll provide these as a service to the regions while holding the standards centrally yourself.
 
Key Responsibilities include but not limited to: 
  • Define and own the sales methodology, pipeline stages and stage exit criteria
  • Separate and clarify the account management versus new business development motions
  • Own pricing, quoting and discount governance, including approval workflows and audit trails
  • Act as the single owner of the CRM and the wider sales tech stack
  • Deliver pipeline visibility, velocity tracking, forecasting and win or loss analysis that leadership can trust and roll up nationally
  • Own standardised customer facing reporting so it is produced consistently rather than hand built by individual reps
  • Provide rep and branch performance dashboards giving leadership and reps a consistent view of performance
  • Design, administer and continuously improve commission plans and quotas nationally, in partnership with Finance and Payroll
  • Handle disputes and plan changes fairly and consistently
  • Lead handling quotes, proposals, and contract and order processing
About You
  • Experience in sales operations, revenue operations or a closely related commercial function, ideally from a multi region, field based B2B business
  • Proven ability to operate neutrally across competing regional or divisional interests, holding central standards while still being seen as a service partner rather than head office overreach
  • Strong command of CRM platforms and the wider sales tech stack, with the judgement to prioritise a roadmap across competing regional demands
  • Genuine analytical fluency, comfortable owning forecasting, pipeline analytics and reporting, and translating data into decisions leadership will actually act on
  • A builder's mindset, able to stand up a function from a phased starting point and perform several pillars personally before scaling a team under you
  • Excellent stakeholder management, with the credibility to influence regional leaders and present confidently to executive and board audiences
Key Benefits
  • A newly created, high visibility role.
  • A genuine mandate to build a national function from the ground up, not inherit someone else's half finished version of it
  • Based in Homebush with a small, dedicated team from day one.
  • Broad exposure across systems, commercial strategy, finance and executive stakeholders, with a clear path to shape how the whole sales organisation operates
  • Attractive salary package 
  • Hybrid work environment

job.title: Head of Finance
job.description:
About The Company 
 
Our client is a fast growing, Australian brand with a genuine global footprint. With Australia representing around a third of the business and the remainder spread across international markets, this is a company that manufactures its own products, sells predominantly through wholesale channels, and continues to expand into new territories. Backed by venture capital, the business is in a genuine growth and change phase, and this is your opportunity to be a key part of that next stage.
 
We are seeking an experienced, hands on Head of Finance to lead the finance function and play a central role in the commercial direction of the business. 
 
About The Role 
 
You will lead a small, highly experienced finance team, take ownership of all financial reporting and analysis, and act as a genuine business partner to the leadership team on the big picture decisions shaping the company's growth. 
 
Key responsibilities include:
  • Preparing and presenting monthly board reporting to VC and investor stakeholders
  • Consolidating financial reporting across multiple business entities
  • Overseeing costing and product costing, including raw materials, cost of goods and inventory holding
  • Deliver budgeting, forecasting, reporting and commercial analysis
  • Managing multi-currency, multi-customer forecasting across a largely international customer base
  • Utilising AI tools and platforms to enhance forecasting, stock planning and reporting efficiency
  • Drive improvements across processes, controls, reporting and automation
  • Providing commercial support on supplier negotiations, capital investment and growth initiatives
About You
 
To succeed in this role you will bring proven, hands on experience in a similar consumer goods environment, ideally retail, beauty, fashion or a closely aligned industry.
  • CA/CPA qualified 
  • Prior experience in a Head of Finance, or similar senior finance role within a consumer goods, retail, beauty, fashion or manufacturing business
  • Demonstrated experience preparing and presenting board reports, ideally gained within a VC backed, private equity backed, or listed business environment
  • Strong technical accounting and reporting skills, with the ability to consolidate reporting across multiple entities
  • Direct experience with inventory builds, product costing, bills of materials and manufacturing cost structures
  • High AI literacy and comfort adopting new technology and reporting tools
  • Excellent communication skills, with the confidence to engage in commercial discussions with international investors and stakeholders
  • The maturity and commercial acumen to operate at a senior level, balancing detail with big picture thinking
Key Benefits: 
  • This is a rare opportunity to join a genuinely exciting, homegrown Australian brand at an important stage of its growth.
  • You will work closely with an engaged and commercially minded leadership team
  • Be part of a company that is building something significant on the global stage
  • Hybrid working 
  • Attractive Salary Package + Bonus
